recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. No core FHIR follow-up is needed for FHIR-17688; changing the current text would duplicate applied guidance or risk undoing the later FHIR-18356 clarification.
issue_request: FHIR-17688 was a Published, Persuasive with Modification FHIR-I issue asking to reconcile mixed SHALL/SHOULD/MAY narrative language. Its final resolution said the modifier-extension wording was already partly addressed and requested changing the fallback sentence to: "Resource instances that permit narrative SHOULD always contain narrative to support human-consumption as a fallback".
initial_application: Commit 98d8515d02da7984b3881dd53b042cf870d34e34 first qualified the conformance-rules is-modifier narrative requirement for GF#17688 after FHIR-I Zulip discussion. Commit f283fcb089a0b386ec4c026fa45ef060998defb4 then changed source/narrative.html to the exact requested fallback wording. FHIR-16423 commit fe5743607404d3b80d049da7a8fde4dc85be2d5d supplied the modifier-extension status wording that FHIR-17688 cited as already partly addressed.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini actively lists Narrative and maps the narrative type page, so source/narrative.html and source/datatypes/narrative.xml are build-scoped. Later Published issue FHIR-18356 intentionally narrowed the narrative page modifier-extension prose to elements described by the narrative, while the Narrative.status code definition still says the narrative SHALL reflect all modifier extensions.
reconciliation: No source edit was made. Current source/narrative.html has the exact requested "Resource instances that permit narrative" sentence, current source/conformance-rules.html has the qualified generated/other-status is-modifier narrative language, and current source/datatypes/narrative.xml preserves the modifier-extension status rule.

related_jiras.note: Published modifier-extension issue that added the Narrative.status = extensions SHALL language cited by FHIR-17688 as already partly addressed.
